full_judgment:
Surendra Kumar Sinha CJ. These appeals by leave are directed from a judgment of the High Court Division in a First Appeal arose out of Title Suit No.47 of 2004. Md. Shakhawat Hossain and Abdur Rahman, the respondents, instituted two suits for declaration of title in respect of .67 acre out of 1.77 acres of land in S.A. Plot No.834 of S. A. Khatian No.65. 

 2. Plaint Case is that the suit land belonged to Nishi Kanta Roy and Pran Kanta Roy who took settlement of the said land from Kashimpur Zaminder namely Sarada Prasad Roy Chowdhury and others. They sold 3.46½ acres of land to Dulu Ram Barman and Rada Mohan Barman on 15.11.1951 who, in turn, sold 3.30 acres of land to Md. Elimuddin and Md. Manik Miah by deed dated 16.03.1954. S.A. record of right was prepared in their names. Md. Elimuddin transferred 1.77 acres of land to Abdul Mazid Mia on 11.04.1966, who after purchase, got possession, mutated his name in the khatian and paid rent to the government. Said Abdul Mazid transferred 1.77 acres of land to Iftekharuddin Ahmed by two registered deeds dated 28.04.1988 and 05.05.1988 and delivered possession, who also mutated his name and paid rent to the government. Said Iftekharuddin Ahmed transferred the suit land along with some other land to his company namely East West International Company Limited by deed dated 03.12.1992 and delivered possession. The Company executed a Power of Attorney in favour of Iftekharuddin Ahmed on 10.07.1993 on the strength of which he transferred the suit land to his sons Aneek Intesar Ahmed and khondoker Samsul Alam Pokraj by deed dated 14.01.2003. The Defendant No. 4 filed a complaint under section 26(1 A) of the Forest Act against the Shamsul Alam Pokraj being Forest Case No. 240/1998 in the Court of Magistrate. The Magistrate considering the materials on record discharged the accused. The Defendant No.2, Divisional Forest officer filed objection Case No.145/68 before the Assistant Settlement Officer which was rejected. Aneek Intesar Ahmed left abroad and before that he executed a Power of Attorney in favour of Iftekharuddin. Shamsul Alam and Aneek transferred the suit land to the plaintiffs by a deed dated 09.06.2004. Plaintiffs came to know that the suit had been recorded in the name of Divisional Forest Officer in R.S. Khatian No.2. 

 5. The point in controversy has a limited compass. If the suit land is reserved forest the suit instituted by the respondents will be barred by law. There is no dispute that the suit land belonged to the predecessors of the respondents. In view of such admitted position, the onus lies upon the government to show that the suit land has been acquired by the government as reserved forest. In Title Suit Nos.47 and 48 of 2004, the plaintiffs are claiming title in respect of S.A. Plot No.834 under Kouchakuri mouza No. 414. In Title Suit No.56 of 2004 the government is claiming title in plot No.834 of S.A. Khatian No.1/29 measuring 15.20 acres belonging to Dhankure Acquired Group of wards Estate and also by gazette notification No.3125/Forest dated 13.4.55 as acquired reserved forest. In all the suits the suit plot is 834 under Kouchakuri Mouza. The High Court Division held that by successive transfers the private plaintiffs acquired title and possession of the suit land and that though there was proposal for acquisition of the suit plot as reserved forest, it was not ultimately acquired as reserved forest upon compliance of formalities.
